svg.title: Nested containers: one e-mail, one archive, two members
svg.desc: Containment tree of an e-mail with an encrypted archive attachment holding a document and a script; what goes down (passwords, depth, budgets) and what comes back up (member summaries, worst-member evidence, incomplete reasons).

g.text: depth 0 (top-level file)
depth 1 (attachment)
depth 2 (archive members)
What comes back up, per level
invoice.eml (MailHandler: ContainerLayer 'mail')
Sender checks (SPF / DKIM / DMARC from the top Authentication-Results), display-name spoof,
reply-to, deceptive links, risky attachment names. The body becomes ctx.text for prompt-guard and the
LLM. "Password: 4471" in the body is offered to the archive below.
invoice.eml!/docs.zip (ArchiveHandler: 'archive')
Opened into a private temp folder by ContainerExtractor: password tried from the message, then
common ones; zip-slip and device names refused; nested archives expanded by the extractor itself
(archive_max_depth 3); 100 MB total, 500 entries, ratio 100x; risky members get the scan budget
(archive_scan_members 25) first.
...docs.zip!/report.docm
Full pipeline at depth 2: macro (olevba), YARA, integrity, prompt-guard,
relationships, QR, ML, LLM. Its own containers would only be listed: depth
2 = max_nesting.
...docs.zip!/pay.js
Full pipeline at depth 2: script categories (download, execute, recovery...),
obfuscation, YARA. Emulation only if enabled (off by default; it runs the
script in box-js).
Member summary
name, verdict, risk_score, hashes, first 8 indicators, scan_status; archive flags
(double extension, RTLO, executable) attached.
Worst-member evidence
the member with the highest risk score: its contributions are copied into the
container's signal (.worst) and re-scored with a prefix:
archive_member:macro_autoexec, then mail_attachment:archive_member:...
Completeness
each member's incomplete_reasons join ctx.member_reasons; the container
takes the most severe status: failed > locked > partial > unsupported > complete.
An encrypted member never opened is 'locked'.
Provenance
what members sent outside (provenance.shared) is listed with member_path.
In a worker
for the top-level file only, the worker reports 'container' (its own findings) and
'member' (each direct member done), so a time-out keeps them as partial
evidence.
Limits that stop the descent: max_nesting 2 (members of a depth-2 container are listed, not scanned); per-container scan budgets (archive 25, mail 25, web 5, embedded
25); mail_max_attachments 50 and the shared 100 MB byte budget. Every member left out becomes an incomplete reason, so the top-level result reads 'partial' (or 'locked'),
never plain 'complete'.
scan_file(attachment, depth 1)
scan_file(member, depth 2)
Nested containers: one e-mail, one archive, two members
Illustrative inert example; behaviour read from engine/containers.py and detectors/container_extractor.py at commit d45715a.
